title: My Favorite Budget Laptop Is $550 Off Its Retail Price Today
gist: A deal post on the HP OmniBook 5 at $750, 42 percent off a $1,300 retail price, framed against the reviewer's observation that budget laptops now cost hundreds more than six months ago. The substantive signals are Qualcomm Snapdragon X silicon delivering MacBook-class battery life in sub-$750 Windows machines, OLED panels reaching the budget tier, and permanent deep discounting that makes the stated retail price largely fictional.

insights.claim: Laptops recommended for budget-conscious shoppers now cost hundreds of dollars more than they did six months ago, according to a reviewer who tests the category continuously.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Rapid ASP inflation in the entry tier is a real-time read on component or tariff cost pass-through in consumer PCs, ahead of official price indices.
insights.quote: Many of my favorite laptops to recommend for budget-conscious shoppers are hundreds more today than they were six months ago.

insights.claim: The HP OmniBook 5 is frequently discounted well below its $1,300 stated retail price and currently sells at $750, indicating the list price functions as an anchor rather than a real transaction price.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Permanent deep discounting means reported PC ASPs overstate realized revenue per unit — margin at HP's consumer tier is thinner than list pricing suggests.
insights.quote: Don't let the retail price of $1,300 throw you off, either.
insights.locator: Then there's the HP OmniBook 5 to save the day

themes.theme: Qualcomm Arm silicon in the value tier

insights.claim: The discounted OmniBook 5 configuration uses a Qualcomm Snapdragon X Plus chip and delivers long-lasting battery life comparable to a MacBook, while HP also ships Intel and AMD versions of the same chassis.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Qualcomm winning the battery-life comparison inside a tri-sourced chassis is direct evidence of Arm share capture from Intel and AMD in Windows laptops.
insights.quote: the Qualcomm model gets you long-lasting battery life, akin to what you get on a MacBook
insights.locator: Importantly, this is also the model

insights.claim: The cheaper HP OmniBook 3 with a Snapdragon X chip is slightly less powerful but gets even better battery life and is called the best laptop available under $600, showing Arm silicon has reached the sub-$600 price band.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Arm penetration into the sub-$600 tier expands Qualcomm's PC volume base beyond premium halo devices, where x86 margins are most defensible.
insights.quote: But it's easily the best laptop you can buy for under $600.
insights.locator: if you're looking for an even deeper discount

themes.theme: Panel and build spec migration downmarket

insights.claim: A 14-inch OLED panel with 16 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage now ships at a $750 street price, with color range that the reviewer says blows typical IPS displays at that price out of the water.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: OLED reaching the $750 Windows tier compresses the premium display differentiator and pressures panel pricing for LCD suppliers.
insights.locator: This configuration has a 14-inch OLED screen

insights.claim: The 16-inch OmniBook 5 sells for $650, less than the 14-inch, but drops the touchscreen and stretches the same 1920 x 1200 resolution across a larger panel — an inverted size-price relationship driven by spec downgrades.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Larger-but-cheaper SKUs signal OEMs clearing panel inventory by spec-stripping rather than cutting margin on the flagship configuration.
insights.locator: There's also a discount on the 16-inch model

insights.claim: The OmniBook 5's persistent weakness is a poor touchpad, which the reviewer says is typical of cheap touchpads but harder to excuse with the MacBook Neo in the market.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Input hardware remains the durable Apple advantage that spec-matched Windows machines cannot close on price alone.
insights.quote: It has a crappy touchpad that is no fun to use.
insights.locator: There's really just one major problem
